questions.prompt: What is the single most impactful check that `strict` turns on?

options.text: strictNullChecks — it keeps null/undefined out of other types

questions.explanation: strictNullChecks prevents null/undefined from silently entering other types, eliminating a huge class of 'cannot read property of undefined' bugs.

questions.prompt: What does `noEmit` do, and when is it used?

options.text: It type-checks without producing JavaScript — used in bundler-based apps where the bundler emits code and tsc only checks

questions.explanation: noEmit runs the full type check but writes no .js, so tsc acts purely as a checker alongside a bundler.

questions.prompt: What does `isolatedModules` guarantee, and who needs it?

options.text: That files never import each other
That every file can be transpiled on its own; bundlers like esbuild/SWC that compile file-by-file require it
That the output is a single file

questions.explanation: isolatedModules ensures each file is transpilable in isolation, which single-file transpilers (esbuild, SWC, Babel) rely on.

options.text: No — it's a separate, recommended option that makes arr[i]/obj[key] include undefined

questions.explanation: noUncheckedIndexedAccess is opt-in (not in strict). It adds undefined to indexed access results, forcing you to handle out-of-range/missing keys.

questions.prompt: The compiler option that emits nothing but still type-checks is ______. (the option name)
questions.explanation: noEmit type-checks without writing output — the standard way bundler-based apps run tsc in CI.

options.text: Building multiple interdependent tsconfig projects in the right order and rebuilding only what changed

questions.explanation: Project references (composite + references) organize large multi-project builds, compiling dependencies in order and incrementally.
